new_entities.name: DGL licorice
new_entities.description: Deglycyrrhizinated licorice preparations used as upper-gastrointestinal remedies, including standardized flavonoid-rich extracts with reduced glycyrrhizin content.

new_entities.name: Reflux symptoms
new_entities.description: Patient-reported symptoms of gastroesophageal reflux, especially heartburn, regurgitation, and related quality-of-life impairment.

edges.population: adults with gastroesophageal reflux or upper-GI symptom syndromes using licorice-based nonprescription products
edges.mechanism: Deglycyrrhizinated licorice extracts are proposed to soothe the esophageal and gastric mucosa and may exert anti-inflammatory effects, but many products combine licorice with other actives and the clinically dominant mechanism remains uncertain.
edges.summary: Licorice-based reflux products have more real trial data than many supplement users realize, but the evidence is still product-specific rather than definitive. The best modern placebo-controlled reflux trial is positive, yet other supportive studies blend licorice with additional ingredients or target broader dyspepsia rather than classic GERD.
edges.caveats: This edge reflects deglycyrrhizinated or low-glycyrrhizin licorice products, not ordinary licorice candy. Some supporting evidence uses multi-ingredient gums or dyspepsia outcomes rather than isolated reflux endpoints.
